summary: This PR adds backfill_phase_self_report.py (with a real, subprocess-driven regression test suite) to close a genuine, well-documented recurring gap -- workers merging PRs (#559, #560) without updating their own phase-plan self-report -- by having software independently confirm a real merge via `gh pr view`/`gh pr list` and mechanically patch the exact status/completed_by_task/evidence fields, wired into both the tier1 merge path (supervisor-entrypoint.sh) and the tier2 cron sweep (auto_phase_continuation.py). It also documents an audit-check CI-timing-race fix as a patch file for supervisor-entrypoint.sh, which lives outside this repo's git tracking -- confirmed consistent with this repo's established convention of shipping such changes as unapplied .diff files under ai-os/patches/ (17 prior examples exist for the same file), so this is not a process violation, but it does mean the audit-rerun logic and the new backfill call-site wiring are not live until a human applies the patch on the server. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. Diff stat and content are consistent with tier1 (additive scripts/tests, no migrations/schema/auth/security paths, no heavy deletion). Subprocess calls use list-arg exec (no shell injection) and pass JSON via env vars rather than interpolating into python -c strings as the author notes. The phase-block matching logic correctly handles both real on-disk schemas (`- id: <string>` and 2-space-indented `- phase: <int>`), verified by a test built from an actual production-data bug the author caught. Approving, but flagging real gaps below for follow-up rather than blocking on them, since the mechanism is best-effort/non-fatal and degrades to the pre-existing status quo (a human eventually notices a missing self-report) rather than introducing a new failure mode.
issues: No locking around the shared REPO_ROOT git checkout (/opt/veridian/repos/claude-control): sync_repo_root() does `git reset --hard origin/master` and commit_and_push() later does add/commit/push against the same working tree, with no mutex. This script can run concurrently from two independent triggers -- supervisor-entrypoint.sh firing per tier1 merge (2-3 concurrent workers per the standing doc) and auto_phase_continuation.py's 30-minute cron sweep iterating many tasks -- so two invocations can race: one process's reset can land mid-read of another's `lines = f.readlines()`, and a concurrent `git push origin master` can be rejected non-fast-forward. This exact class of shared-mutable-state bug was previously found and fixed with file locking for CONTROLLER.yaml/task.yaml per SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md; this new script doesn't adopt that pattern.

Failures are swallowed silently: supervisor-entrypoint.sh's call site uses `|| true` and the sweep loop only logs to stderr/supervisor.log, so a push race, a not-found plan file, or an unresolvable phase id look identical in outcome to 'nothing needed backfilling' -- there's no escalation path distinguishing a real failure from a no-op, which partially undercuts the goal of never again needing a human to notice a silent gap.

The supervisor-entrypoint.sh changes (both the audit-check rerun block and the new backfill call-site) ship only as an unapplied ai-os/patches/*.diff file, consistent with this repo's existing convention for that untracked, server-only script, but the audit-rerun behavior and the tier1 backfill wiring are not actually live until a human/process applies that patch on the server -- worth confirming this happens as part of merging this PR, not assumed.

Minor: patch_phase_block() only overwrites an existing `status:` field: if a phase entry has no status key at all, it will never insert one (only completed_by_task/evidence get inserted when absent), so block_self_reports_done() would keep returning False and the script would keep attempting (harmless no-op commits) on every run for that entry. Low severity since both real on-disk schemas encountered always carry a status field.
